faq.q: Is MOV to MP4 conversion lossless?
faq.a: When the codecs are compatible, yes – the streams are copied without re-encoding.

faq.q: Are my videos uploaded?
faq.a: No. Everything runs on your device with WebCodecs; nothing is sent to a server.

faq.q: Is there a size limit?
faq.a: Files are processed in memory, so practical size is about 1–2 GB on desktop and 300–500 MB on phones. AVI, WMV and FLV inputs are not supported. Chrome, Edge and Safari 16.4+ have the required WebCodecs; Firefox 130+ works for most files.

faq.q: Is there a watermark?
faq.a: Never. No sign-up, no watermark and no daily limits.

faq.q: Can I make the file smaller at the same time?
faq.a: Yes – choose 1080p, 720p or 480p and a lower quality level, or use Compress Video.

faq.q: Why does my browser say it cannot encode?
faq.a: Some browsers lack certain encoders (e.g. H.264 on Linux Chromium builds). Try Chrome or Edge, or pick WebM output.

guide.intro: MOV is Apple’s QuickTime container used by iPhones, Macs and many cameras. MP4 is the universal video container that plays on every phone, TV, browser and editor. Converting lets you play, edit or upload the video anywhere – and {brand} does it without uploading gigabytes to a server.
uses: Make MOV recordings play on TVs, phones and editors that expect MP4.
Upload videos to sites that reject your current format.
Re-wrap camera or screen recordings without losing quality.
Batch convert a folder of clips.
tips: Leave resolution on Keep and quality High for a fast, lossless re-wrap when possible.
Plug in your laptop – hardware encoding is faster on mains power.
Use Trim Video first if you only need part of the clip.
more: How it works

{brand} reads the MOV container with Mediabunny (MPL-2.0) and, when the video is already H.264/H.265 and the audio AAC, simply re-wraps the streams into MP4 without re-encoding – lossless and many times faster than real time. Otherwise it re-encodes with your browser’s hardware WebCodecs encoder.
Honest limits

Files are processed in memory, so practical size is about 1–2 GB on desktop and 300–500 MB on phones. AVI, WMV and FLV inputs are not supported. Chrome, Edge and Safari 16.4+ have the required WebCodecs; Firefox 130+ works for most files.
Compared with other converters
CloudConvert, Convertio and FreeConvert upload your file, cap free use (often 1 GB or a few conversions per day) and queue jobs. Here conversion starts instantly, offline, with no account.

faq.q: Does it keep subtitles and multiple audio tracks?
faq.a: The primary video and audio tracks are converted; extra subtitle tracks are dropped.

faq.q: Does it work on iPhone?
faq.a: Yes on iOS 16.4+ in Safari, for files up to a few hundred MB.

Files are processed in memory, so practical size is about 1–2 GB on desktop and 300–500 MB on phones. AVI, WMV and FLV inputs are not supported. Chrome, Edge and Safari 16.4+ have the required WebCodecs; Firefox 130+ works for most files.
Compared with other converters
CloudConvert, Convertio and FreeConvert upload your file, cap free use (often 1 GB or a few conversions per day) and queue jobs. Here conversion starts instantly, offline, with no account.

guide.intro: MKV is the open Matroska container popular for films, OBS recordings and anime releases. WEBM is Google’s open web video format used by browsers, screen recorders and YouTube downloads. Converting lets you play, edit or upload the video anywhere – and {brand} does it without uploading gigabytes to a server.
uses: Make MKV recordings play on TVs, phones and editors that expect WEBM.
Upload videos to sites that reject your current format.
Re-wrap camera or screen recordings without losing quality.
Batch convert a folder of clips.
tips: Leave resolution on Keep and quality High for a fast, lossless re-wrap when possible.
Plug in your laptop – hardware encoding is faster on mains power.
Use Trim Video first if you only need part of the clip.
more: How it works

WebM requires VP8/VP9/AV1 video and Opus/Vorbis audio, so {brand} decodes the MKV and re-encodes it to VP9 + Opus with your browser’s WebCodecs encoder. Speed depends on your device; a 1080p minute takes roughly 30–90 seconds on a modern laptop.
